`devtools::test()` (post-fix): 925 expectations, 0 failures, 0 errors, 9 warnings (all

test, environmental, not code-related), 1 skip (a `DECIPHER`-present environment skip).
(The original draft's preamble reported 935 expectations for the pre-fix baseline; a
same-day CLAUDE.md session note independently recorded 925 as the correct baseline after
an unrelated same-day `absolute_fit_pvalue` removal -- the draft's 935 appears to have been
a stale/incorrect count, not a regression introduced by this session's fixes, none of
which added or removed a test.)
`devtools::check()` (`--no-tests`, tests run separately above): **0 errors, 0 warnings,
0 notes -- Status: OK.** The one packaging-level `R CMD build` warning noted in the draft
(auto-detected `R >= 4.1.0` dependency) no longer appears -- see finding 7 below.
`lintr::lint_package()`: 214 lints package-wide (down from 226), **0 in `R/`** (down from
12 -- see findings 1-2 below); the remainder are pre-existing `tests/`/`inst/workflows/`
lints, out of scope for this review. Non-ASCII sweep of `R/`: clean, zero hits (unchanged).

# Code Review

Purpose: To produce high quality code that is well written and organized according to
best coding practices.

### [x] Functionality: readable, organized, consistent across all 28 files.

Roxygen documentation, internal-helper naming (`.` prefix), `package::function()`
cross-package calls, and the coarse-to-fine `rank_system` convention are applied
consistently everywhere. The statistical core (`train.R`/`evaluate.R`/`score_collapse.R`/
`restore_hierarchy.R`/`regional_overlap.R`/`support_curves.R`) is unusually
well-commented for *why*, not just *what* -- most non-obvious formulas carry an inline
derivation or a pointer to the real dataset that motivated them. No changes needed here.

### [x] Optimizations: no new performance concerns; two small DRY opportunities noted under Coding standards, both fixed.

No new efficiency issues found. This package's own session history already shows
several real, measured performance fixes (the `align_cache`/`.seq_matrix_partner_index()`
memoization in `restore_hierarchy.R`/`regional_overlap.R`, found via real ~590x and
~100x speedups on real 13,442-observation data) -- nothing found this pass regresses
or duplicates that work. The two duplicated-code patterns noted under Coding standards
below were style/maintainability items, not measured performance problems; both are now
factored into shared helpers (findings 4 and 5).

### [x] Coding standards: all findings fixed this session; no correctness impact.

**`.lintr`'s `R/train.R` `object_name_linter` exclusion line numbers had drifted (Low,
mechanical fix -- Fixed).** The exclusion previously read
`"R/train.R" = list(object_name_linter = c(864, 899, 984, 1000, 1008))`, but a live
`lintr::lint_package()` run found the real `H1_Lookup`/`H2_Lookup`/`H2`/`H3` object-name
lints (the ones this exclusion is meant to cover, per its own comment: "mirror the
taxa_model_params object's own documented slot names") sitting at lines 900, 935, 1075,
1091, 1099 before any fix in this session was applied. *Fixed:* updated to those 5 values
-- then, because finding 2's own `train.R` fix (wrapping the 143-char line, finding 2)
inserted one additional line earlier in the file, re-ran `lintr::lint_package()` a second
time immediately before finalizing `.lintr` (per this exact finding's own caution) and
found all 5 had shifted again, by exactly +1: `c(901, 936, 1076, 1092, 1100)`. That is the
value now in `.lintr`. A final `lintr::lint_package()` run confirms 0 `object_name_linter`
hits (or any other lint) remain in `R/train.R`.

**Six other real, cosmetic `R/` lints (Low, mechanical fixes -- Fixed):**

- `R/evaluate.R:651` -- `brace_linter`, "Wrap multi-line function bodies in curly braces"

  `{ }`.
- `R/support_curves.R:256` -- `brace_linter`, same "both or neither" issue
  (`species_slot <- if (...) {...} else NULL`). *Fixed:* this file had no other one-line-else
  precedent to follow (only this one occurrence existed), so braces were added to match
  `evaluate.R`'s package-wide convention (both branches braced) rather than removing them
  from the `if`.
- `R/support_curves.R:335` -- `semicolon_linter`: `x <- x[ok]; y <- y[ok]` (inside

- `R/train.R:714` -- `line_length_linter`, 143 characters (limit 120). *Fixed:* wrapped the

All six were re-confirmed lint-clean individually and via a final full-package
`lintr::lint_package()` run (0 hits anywhere in `R/`); none of these six edits shifted any
other, previously-clean line into a new lint.

**`df` used as a local variable name, shadowing `stats::df()` (Low, informational --
Fixed).** `build_sequence_matrix()` (`R/build_sequence.R`), `trim_to_amplicon()`
(`R/trim_to_amplicon.R`), and `read_crabs_output()` (`R/read_crabs.R`) each had a local
`df` data-frame variable. *Fixed:* renamed per-file, chosen to reflect what each variable
actually holds (not a single mechanical find/replace) -- `ref_seqs` in
`build_sequence.R` (the working reference-sequence table being cleaned/deduplicated/
filtered/thinned before alignment), `seq_df` in `trim_to_amplicon.R` (the working copy of
`reference_df` whose `sequence` column is progressively replaced with extracted
amplicons), `crabs_df` in `read_crabs.R` (the raw parsed CRABS table, before the final
`reference_df` object is assembled from it at the end of the function). Renamed via
exact-scope, word-boundary-safe substitution (confirmed the pattern never matched inside
the unrelated `reference_df` parameter name, which shares the `df` substring). Each `df`
was confirmed function-local before renaming, and no test in `tests/testthat/` references
any of these variables by name (they are local to their respective functions and never
exposed).

**Two real DRY opportunities (Low-Medium, informational -- both Fixed, with one real
behavioral discrepancy found and preserved rather than silently normalized).**
1. `R/coverage.R`'s `.audit_one_genus_reverse()` had two near-identical ~25-line blocks
   for NCBI-taxonomy-subtree species enumeration (the "2. Primary source" NCBI branch and
   the "3. Fallback" branch). *Fixed:* extracted into a new shared internal helper,
   `.ncbi_species_enumerate(genus_uid, grp, warn_on_error)` (`@noRd`, placed immediately
   above `.audit_one_genus_reverse()`), called from both sites. **Read both blocks
   carefully before merging, per this finding's own explicit caution, and found they were
   NOT behaviorally identical**: the primary-source block's `tryCatch()` error handler
   called `warning()` naming the genus and the underlying error message on failure; the
   fallback block's error handler silently returned `character(0L)` on failure, with no
   warning at all. This is a real, intentional-looking asymmetry (the fallback only runs
   after the primary GBIF path already came back empty, so a second silent failure there
   avoids doubling up warnings for what the caller already knows was an unproductive
   lookup) -- preserved exactly via the new `warn_on_error` parameter (`TRUE` at the
   primary-source call site, `FALSE` at the fallback site) rather than silently picking one
   behavior for both. Every other aspect of the two blocks (search term, batching, retry
   absence, field extraction, `is_plausible_binomial()` filtering, return shape) was
   confirmed identical before extraction.
2. `R/fetch.R` had four separate hand-rolled retry loops with the identical
   `attempt <- 0L; success <- FALSE; while (attempt < 3L && !success) { ... Sys.sleep(attempt)
   ... }` shape: `.fetch_summaries_batched()`, `.fetch_taxonomy_map()`,
   `.fetch_fasta_batched()`, `.fetch_locations_batched()`. *Fixed:* extracted into a new
   shared internal helper, `.retry_fetch(fn, max_attempts = 3L)` (`@noRd`), which retries a
   zero-argument closure (one fetch+parse attempt) and returns `list(value, success)`.
   **Confirmed, not assumed, that all four loops were genuinely identical** in max attempts
   (3, hardcoded), backoff (linear `Sys.sleep(attempt)`, no sleep after the final attempt),
   and error handling (silent on exhaustion -- no warning or error is raised if every
   attempt fails; the caller's pre-allocated slot for that batch simply stays at its initial
   empty value) before merging -- unlike finding 4 above, no behavioral difference needed
   preserving here. Each of the four call sites now builds its per-batch closure and checks
   `result$success` before assigning into its accumulator (`res[[i]]`/`chunks[i]`), which
   correctly leaves that slot at its original pre-allocated value (`NULL` for the list
   accumulators, `""` for `chunks`, a plain character vector) on exhaustion -- exactly
   matching the original code's behavior, which never assigned into the slot at all on
   failure.

**`interpret_model()`'s reused `mu_score`/`mu_gap` names created a fragile,
non-obvious scoping dependency (Low -- Fixed via rename).** In `R/interpret.R`, the outer
scalars `mu_score <- model_params$H1_Global_Mu[["score_logit"]]` and
`mu_gap <- model_params$H1_Global_Mu[["gap_logit"]]` shared a name with `H1_Lookup`'s real
per-species columns `mu_score`/`mu_gap`, which the "Per-species thresholds" block's
`dplyr::mutate()` relies on shadowing via tidy-eval data-mask precedence. *Fixed:* renamed
the two outer scalars to `global_mu_score`/`global_mu_gap` everywhere they're used in the
"Hypothesis baselines"/"Global H1 profile" sections (the scalar declarations themselves,
`mean_score_pct`/`runner_up_pct`, `h2_logit`/`h3_logit`, and the `global_h1` data frame).
Per the task's explicit instruction, `H1_Lookup`'s actual `mu_score`/`mu_gap` columns were
**not** renamed (a real, documented, ecosystem-wide column pair used elsewhere in `train.R`
and consumed by other functions -- renaming them would be a breaking change out of scope
here), and the bare `mu_score`/`mu_gap`/`mu_gap` references inside the `dplyr::mutate()`
block itself (lines computing `expected_match_pct`/`danger_gap`/`status`, etc.) were
deliberately left untouched. Verified after the edit: those bare references now
unambiguously resolve to `H1_Lookup`'s per-species columns via `.data`, with no outer
scalar of the same name left in scope to create the collision risk the finding described.

**Packaging: no explicit `Depends: R (>= 4.1.0)` in `DESCRIPTION` (Low-Medium, mechanical
fix -- Fixed).** `R CMD build` previously emitted: *"WARNING: Added dependency on
R >= 4.1.0 because package code uses the pipe `|>` or function shorthand `\(...)`
syntax"*, naming `build_sequence.R`, `calibrate_query_noise.R`, `coverage.R`,
`evaluate.R`, `fetch.R`, `interpret.R`, `train.R`. *Fixed:* added `Depends: R (>= 4.1.0)`
to `DESCRIPTION` directly, placed after `Encoding: UTF-8` and before `Roxygen:`, matching
the field ordering already used in this monorepo's `TaxaTools/DESCRIPTION` (the one
sibling package with its own `Depends:` field). A fresh `devtools::check()` after this
change confirms the `R CMD build` warning no longer appears, and `R CMD check`'s own
Status remains 0/0/0 -- OK.

**`object_usage_linter` hits: all outside `R/`, not a package-code finding (Low,
informational -- unchanged).** Per the task's own instruction to check whether
`object_usage_linter` hits are genuine dead code: all 8 package-wide hits (`no visible
binding for global variable 'true_species'/'p'/'p_true'`) are in
`inst/workflows/calibrate_training_bias_tau.R` (a demonstration/calibration workflow
script, not a `R/` package file) -- `zero` hits in `R/` itself, both before and after this

### [x] Automated tests: confirmed passing when run locally.

`devtools::test()`: 925 expectations, 0 failures, 0 errors. 9 warnings, all deliberate
(8 are `assign_scores(score_type = "none")` tests asserting the "scores will be ignored"
warning fires; 1 is an S4-dispatch environmental warning from `pwalign`/`Biostrings`
inside a `.check_regional_overlap()` test, not a code issue). 1 skip (an
environment-dependent skip: `DECIPHER` is installed here, so the "errors when DECIPHER
absent" test correctly skips itself). None of the 9 fixes in this session added or

not bare `testthat::test_dir()`, per this ecosystem's own documented footgun.)

### [x] Vulnerabilities: none found.

Checked for the four ecosystem-relevant patterns flagged in the task brief, plus the
standard sweep:
- **SSRF / "host taken from untrusted external data" (the TaxaFetch DataONE
  precedent).** `fetch.R`'s NCBI (`rentrez`), BOLD (`.bold_api_base`, a hardcoded
  constant), and `coverage.R`'s Xeno-canto/iNaturalist calls all target fixed, hardcoded
  hosts. The one place a value returned by a third-party API feeds back into a request
  URL -- `.bold_fetch_documents(query_id)`, where `query_id` comes from BOLD's own
  `query/preprocessor`/`query` response -- inserts it only as a **path segment**
  (`httr2::req_url_path_append("documents", query_id, "download")`) on the fixed
  `.bold_api_base` host; `req_url_path_append()` cannot be used to substitute a different
  scheme or host, so this cannot redirect the request off BOLD's own domain. Not
  analogous to TaxaFetch's SSRF case (which took a *full URL, host included* from
  third-party EML metadata with no allowlist).
- **Unsafe deserialization.** Every `readRDS()` call (checkpoint/cache files under
  `tools::R_user_dir("TaxaLikely", "cache")` or a caller-supplied `cache_dir`) loads only
  files this package's own functions previously wrote via `saveRDS()` with a
  deterministic, hashed filename -- never an arbitrary or externally-supplied `.rds`.
- **Command injection / `system()`/`eval()`/`parse()`.** None found anywhere in the 28
  files.
- **Zip-slip.** Not applicable -- no archive-extraction code in this package.
- **XXE.** `.fetch_taxonomy_map()`/`.fetch_locations_batched()` (`fetch.R`) parse NCBI's
  own XML via `xml2::read_xml()`, which does not resolve external entities by default
  (same conclusion already confirmed live for TaxaFetch's own `xml2` usage).
- **Credentials.** NCBI (`ENTREZ_KEY`/`NCBI_API_KEY`), Xeno-canto (`XC_API_KEY`), and
  iNaturalist (`INAT_API_TOKEN`) keys are all read from environment variables or an
  explicit caller-supplied parameter; no hardcoded credentials anywhere.
- **Path traversal.** Cache/output filenames built from taxon names are sanitized
  (`gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "_", ...)`) before being used in `file.path()`, preventing a
  `..`-bearing taxon string from escaping `cache_dir`. `read_reference_fasta()`/
  `subset_local_database()`/`read_crabs_output()` read a caller-supplied file path
  directly -- expected behavior for a function whose entire job is "read this local file
  the caller pointed at," not a vulnerability under this project's threat model (unlike
  a URL/host taken unrestricted from third-party data).

# Domain Review

Purpose: To ensure the code produces outputs, data, interfaces, or software that is
biologically reasonable when compared to other similar information available.

### [x] Scientific Rigor: no new findings.

Read `TaxaLikely/CLAUDE.md` in full before this pass, per the task's own instruction, to
calibrate against already-settled history -- this package has an unusually deep,
real-data-validated session record (the `sqrt_mismatch` vs. `logit` transform choice,
the `H1_Lookup$sigma_score` squaring bug, per-genus H2 delta/variance shrinkage, the
evidence-ratio crossover gate, the Jeffreys-smoothing + interpolation fix for
`Confusion_Risk_Curves`, the level-aware `calibrate_query_noise()` recalibration). Read
`train.R`, `evaluate.R`, `calibrate.R`, `calibrate_query_noise.R`,
`correct_training_bias.R`, `support_curves.R`, `score_collapse.R`, and
`restore_hierarchy.R` closely, as the task asked, specifically looking for anything
**not** already covered by that history. Spot-checked several roxygen claims against the
actual code rather than trusting the docstring (`build_sequence_matrix()`'s `coverage`
formula; `correct_training_bias()`'s `tau_used = 0` fallback arithmetic;
`assign_scores()`'s H2/H3 congener-median anchoring; `unreferenced_candidates()`'s
`score_original = NA` on added rows) -- all matched the code exactly. Found no new
scientific-rigor defect. The one remaining documented-but-unfixed simplification (H3's
delta is `H2$delta + 2.0` as a flat, non-genus-specific heuristic "one additional
taxonomic step," explicitly flagged in the code's own comment as a possible future
extension) is pre-existing, already disclosed, and not something this pass is treating
as a new finding. None of the 9 fixes applied this session touch any statistical/domain
logic -- all are cosmetic, refactoring, packaging, or debris-cleanup fixes with confirmed
identical behavior (or, for finding 4, a preserved, parameterized behavioral difference).

### [x] Outputs: no new findings.

No output-comparability issues found. `evaluate_likelihoods()`'s `raw_likelihood` vs.
`score_likelihood` (ratio-normalized) distinction, and the `score_likelihood_cov`/
`score_likelihood_evidence` parallel columns, are documented accurately and match their
implementation (score-only sigma inflation for `_cov`, the closed-form crossover-gated
rescale for `_evidence`) on direct reading.

### [x] Algorithms: no new findings; existing design choices are internally consistent.

Verified, by direct reading rather than assumption, that `score_transform` (`"logit"` vs.
`"sqrt_mismatch"`) is threaded consistently end to end: `.prep_training_data()`,
`train_likelihood_model()`'s H1/H2/H3 fitting, `.evaluate_one_query()`'s density
evaluation, and `calibrate_query_noise()`'s residual computation all read
`model_params$Score_Transform` (or receive it explicitly) rather than hardcoding
`"logit"` anywhere in the inference path -- confirming the Session 158 fix is complete,
not partially applied. Verified the Empirical-Bayes shrinkage weight `w = n/(n +
prior_weight)` is applied with the same form and the same `prior_weight` source
(`model_params$Stats$prior_weight`, not the true pooled count) everywhere it's used:
H1 species means (`train.R`), H2 per-genus delta/variance (`train.R`), the
`Confusion_Risk_Curves` per-genus/per-family rate curves (`support_curves.R`), and the
Monte Carlo mean-uncertainty term (`evaluate.R`) -- consistent, not reinvented per
call site. Verified the Jeffreys-smoothed (`rate_smooth`/`pooled_rate_smooth`) vs. raw
(`rate`/`pooled_rate`) column split in `support_curves.R` is actually read by the two
different consumers the code comments say it should be (`.lookup_confusion_risk_value()`
reads the smoothed columns; `compute_rank_thresholds()`'s `.youden_best()` reads the raw
`pooled_rate` columns) -- both correct per the file's own stated rationale for keeping
them separate.
